sections.html:
Bartholomew County's seat sits on the East Fork of the White River, around 40 miles south of Indianapolis. People numbered 50,474 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 52,655, spread over about 28.75 square miles.

Owners live in 60.8% of homes. Those homes have a median value of $244,200, while median gross rent is $1,157. There are 21,726 households, averaging 2.34 people. About four in ten homes are rented, which is why landlords and heirs of rental property make up many of the sellers.

Picture a 1950s or 1960s ranch. A buyer using a loan may ask for a new roof, furnace or electrical panel first. A cash buyer sees the same house and subtracts the cost of the work from the price.

Rain exceeding 10 inches fell on June 7, 2008 across watersheds draining into Bartholomew County. The resulting flood did more than $500 million in damage and took three lives. About 2,800 county homes were damaged, which included 15% of every structure in the city, and roughly 1,000 residents sheltered elsewhere.

The Driftwood River, Flatrock River, Clifty Creek and Haw Creek converge here to form the East Fork White River, and about 2,000 square miles of upstream land drains through the area. That keeps flooding among the most significant natural threats.

Planning changed afterward. The city, Columbus Regional Hospital and Cummins paid for their own floodplain study of Haw Creek because the 2008 flooding was worse than FEMA's maps predicted, and the county now has eight stream gauges. City officials also tightened local regulations on the most sensitive part of floodplains.

  • Find out if your lot is mapped as floodplain or floodway.
  • Save flood insurance claims and repair receipts.
  • Disclose any past water in the basement or crawl space.

Everyday weather brings water too, with 47.34 inches of precipitation in an average year. Expect a cash buyer to inspect the foundation, the sump and any stains on basement walls.

Columbus is nicknamed "Athens on the Prairie" for its modern architecture, and seven buildings built between 1942 and 1965 are National Historic Landmarks. Ordinary houses are a different matter. Incorporation as a town came in 1864 and as a city in 1921, so plenty of housing is decades old. Loan-backed buyers often request repairs before closing on homes like that.

Do not spend money on cosmetic fixes before you ask for an offer. With an older house, begin with the roof, gutters, basement and electrical panel, since a buyer's inspector will raise those first.

sections.h2: Who to call for permits and code questions
sections.html:
Several offices share the work, and sellers often call the wrong one. This table shows who handles what.

OfficePhoneWhat it handles
Bartholomew County Department of Technical Code Enforcement812-379-1535Building permits and inspections for new single-family homes, additions and interior remodels
Columbus-Bartholomew County Planning Department812-376-2550Zoning, variances and signs
City of Columbus Code Enforcement812-376-2520Inoperable vehicles, unsafe homes and nuisance properties in the city limits
Engineering Department812-376-2540Storm water, driveways and street access

The city's Development and Building Services page lists each office.

An ordinance from February 2018 applies to every residential rental inside city limits. Owners pay $5 for each parcel, and an application is due within 30 days after a purchase or change of ownership.

Anyone selling a rental should remember that window: the buyer of a rented house has a month to register. Applications go through OpenGov, the city's online system, via Community Development at (812) 376-2520.

Each parcel is counted on its own. An estate that inherits a rental should add registration to its to-do list. See the city's rental registration page for current details.

sections.h2: Employers and moving on short notice
sections.html:
Cummins has its headquarters here and is the largest employer in the region. Research jobs cluster at Infotech Park, and Toyota Material Handling keeps its North American headquarters just south of town. Public schools are run by the Bartholomew Consolidated School Corporation, which has Columbus North and Columbus East high schools.

One big employer can move a housing market. If a plant changes hours or families take transfers, several houses can list together, and a seller who must leave fast finds fewer buyers.

sections.h2: Selling a flood-affected or rental house
sections.html:
Two kinds of Columbus houses come up most often with cash buyers: houses that took water and rentals that need work. For the first, a buyer wants to hear about water in the basement or crawl space, claims you filed and repairs you made, and a lender will ask for the flood zone. For the second, a buyer wants the registration current and any tenant lease in hand.

None of that rules out a quick sale. It does mean the price reflects the condition, so honest information up front saves time. Photographs of repairs, dated receipts and insurance letters all help. If you are unsure which office holds a permit for past work, start with the Technical Code Enforcement office, then the city's Code Enforcement if the question is about a nuisance or unsafe condition.

I-65 passes on the west side of town, U.S. 31 cuts through the northeast, and Indiana Route 46 crosses the south. Five ColumBUS routes operate Monday through Saturday. Indianapolis International Airport lies about 55 miles to the northwest.

Taxes are billed in two halves, usually due May 10 and November 10. A payment up to 30 days late adds 5 percent, and anything later adds 10 percent. A statement listing the upcoming dates reaches you in spring, and the state due dates page has the calendar.

When the house sells, the title company splits the year's taxes between you and the buyer. Request that figure beforehand, then compare it with the settlement statement.

Our process for a Columbus house is short. You send the address and describe the condition. We tour the house and put a cash offer in writing. If you accept, a title company runs the search, drafts the deed and schedules the closing for your date. With no lender involved and clean title work, closing can move fast, and mortgage payoffs and liens come out of your proceeds.

Gather a few papers first: your latest tax statement, your lender's payoff figure, flood insurance records, and the rental registration if tenants live there. A house from an estate needs the court papers and the heirs' names. Offers usually come in under a fully renovated retail sale, so set the number beside what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Columbus, Indiana?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $244,200. Condition and location can put one house far from that figure.

faqs.q: Is Columbus, Indiana at risk of flooding?
faqs.a: In places, yes. The June 2008 flood hit about 15% of all structures in the city. Look up your address on the FEMA flood maps and ask the planning office.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Columbus?
faqs.a: Yes. Every residential rental inside city limits must register under the 2018 ordinance. The fee is $5 a parcel, and you apply within 30 days of buying or changing ownership.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits in Columbus?
faqs.a: For new homes, additions and interior remodels, it is the Bartholomew County Department of Technical Code Enforcement. Zoning questions go to the planning department.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Columbus?
faqs.a: Yes, we buy water-damaged houses as they are. Tell us what you know about the damage and any claim, and we will price the house as it stands.
